title: Lyon §6 arc-collapse merging (q=0 → patch merge)
description:
Lyon §6 ¶1: when an arc's quantization is q=0, the arc collapses (its two endpoints merge into one), and the patches on either side of the arc merge into one larger conforming patch. Paper Table 1 #P counts patches AFTER this merge.

We currently count T-mesh patches (pre-merge). On rocker-arm we get 112 vs paper's 159 — close but the count semantics differ. Without the merge, our 'conforming layout' is denser than the paper's.

Implementation: after Quantization.solve produces q[], walk the T-mesh:
1. Collect zero-quantized arcs Z = { a | q[a] == 0 }.
2. Build patch-adjacency graph (patch p1 adjacent to p2 iff they share a Z arc).
3. Connected components of this graph are the merged conforming patches.
4. Each merged patch's boundary = union of non-Z arcs of its constituent T-patches.
5. Re-emit as QuadLayoutPatch with the merged boundary (still 4 cardinal sides since Z arcs don't change cardinal direction).

Depends on a working ILP (PATCH-85).
definition-of-done: Rocker-arm at α=15° with feasible ILP: post-merge #P matches paper's 159 within ±10%.
testing-plan: Toy: 2x2 patch fixture where one shared arc has q=0 → expect 4 patches → 2 merged patches. Rocker-arm benchmark: report pre-merge vs post-merge #P.
